standard.description: 6 1/2 digit Truevolt digital multimeter, ACAL capable (Keysight data sheet 5991-1983EN)
standard.confidence_text: 95 % (k = 2): the data sheet prints "These specifications are compliant to ISO/IEC 17025 for k = 2" at the head of each model's specification table (5991-1983EN printed p. 13 for the 34461A, p. 15 for the 34465A); it prints no percentage, so 95 % is the coverage probability that goes with k = 2
standard.reference: Keysight Digital Multimeters 34460A/34461A/34465A/34470A data sheet 5991-1983EN, published June 10, 2026, "Specifications 34465A" printed pp. 15-17
standard.author: written by specs/build_34465a_standard.py from the rendered page images of the data sheet

notes.1: SOURCE: Keysight Digital Multimeters 34460A, 34461A, 34465A (6 1/2 digit), 34470A (7 1/2 digit) data sheet 5991-1983EN, published in USA June 10, 2026 (PDF of 28 pages, supplied by the owner as Digital_Multimeters_34460A_34461A_34465A_6__digit_34470A_7__digit.pdf; printed page numbers equal the PDF page numbers). 34465A specifications: pp. 15-17 (DC voltage, resistance, DC current, continuity, diode, DC:DC ratio, temperature: p. 15; true RMS AC voltage, true RMS AC current, capacitance, frequency, burden voltages: p. 16; footnotes: p. 17). Built by the specs builder of this model (shared engine specs/truevolt_standard_engine.py).
notes.2: VERIFICATION: every stored number was read from RENDERED PAGE IMAGES (pdftoppm, 150 dpi for the whole page and 250 dpi for a crop of each table), never from the extracted text, and each stored table was read twice (whole page, then the crop); the two readings agree. The independent second transcription is in the model's test file. Read once only (information in the notes, no lookup uses them): temperature coefficients, gate-time errors, burden voltages, the temperature / continuity / diode / DC ratio lines.
notes.3: CONFIDENCE LEVEL: the data sheet prints "These specifications are compliant to ISO/IEC 17025 for k = 2" at the head of the specification table, and "specifications include measurement uncertainty and were created in compliance with ISO-17025" (p. 28). It prints NO percentage. Stored as confidence_pct 95.0 (k = 2, the coverage probability that belongs to k = 2; repository rule: 95 % -> divisor 2.0, see NOTES.md "Confidence level rule"). The inference k = 2 -> 95 % is the repository's, not a printed figure: FLAG.
notes.4: PERIODS: "90 day", "1 yr" and "2 yr" are stored (three period labels in the free-text period field; no schema change). The printed 24 hour column (relative to calibration standards, footnote 3) is NOT stored. Conditions of the stored columns: 90 day / 1 year / 2 year at the TCAL +/- 5 degC the table heads print: DC voltage and resistance (the first table of p. 15) are printed at TACAL +/- 2 degC (24 hour: +/- 1 degC), TACAL being the temperature of the last ACAL (footnote 1: ACAL run within the last 2 days); the DC current, AC and other functions are at TCAL +/- 5 degC. Footnote 1: specifications are for a 90-minute warm-up, integration setting of 10 or 100 NPLC, auto-zero on, AC slow filter.
notes.5: DEFAULT PERIOD = "1 yr" (owner: the uncertainty assignment uses the 1 year column). StandardSpec.period defaults to "1 yr" for this sheet, so the plain lookup used by the budget (specmanager lookup, tartur.standard_accuracy, uncertainty_budget.build) returns the 1 year figure; for the 34465A that is +/-(0.0030 % of reading + 0.0004 % of the 10 V range) on the 10 V range. The 90 day and 2 year figures are reachable with period="90 day" / "2 yr". A test (tests/test_standard_34465a.py) fails if the default lookup stops returning the 1 yr figure.
notes.6: ACCURACY FORM: +/-(% of reading + % of range). The data sheet does not define "range" for the % of range term; it is taken against the range NAME (100 mV range -> 0.1 V, 10 V -> 10 V, 1 kohm -> 1000 ohm, 100 uA -> 1e-4 A), the Keysight convention and the one the 3458A sheet follows; UNVERIFIED for these data sheets. The value range of each row runs from -full scale to +full scale; footnote 2 of the data sheet: the ranges run 20 % over range (full scale 120 mV, 1.2 V, 12 V, 120 V, 120 ohm ... 1.2 uA ... 1.2 A, 1.2 nF ... 120 uF) EXCEPT 1000 V DC, 750 V AC, the 3 A and 10 A current ranges and the diode test (0 %): those rows end at the range name itself (1000 V, 750 V, 3 A, 10 A).
notes.7: DIRECTION: "input" - the DMM measures (same as the 3458A, 5790B, 8563E and 8902A sheets). specmanager.StandardSpec.lookup defaults to direction "output" and the budget (uncertainty_budget.build) must be asked with direction "input"; tartur.standard_accuracy has the argument. The Datasheet Builder matcher uses the row direction itself.
notes.8: RESOLUTION: no row carries a resolution (the specification tables print none; reading resolution depends on the aperture / NPLC setting). The budget therefore has NO resolution term for this standard; the Standards Specs tab can record one. Reading noise, the gate-time errors and the temperature coefficients are NOT in any stored row.
notes.9: DC VOLTS (p. 15): 100 mV to 1000 V. Temperature coefficient (information, not stored): footnote 6 (non ACAL): add per degC outside the last TACAL +/- 2 degC: 100 mV 0.0005 + 0.0005, 1 V - 1000 V 0.0005 + 0.0001; footnote 7 (with ACAL): add per degC outside TACAL +/- 2 degC: 100 mV 0.0002 + 0.0005, 1 V - 1000 V 0.0002 + 0.0001 (% of reading + % of range). The 1000 V range has no 20 % over range.
notes.10: DC VOLTS 1000 V (footnote 9): for each additional volt over +/-500 V add 0.02 mV of error. NOT in the stored 1000 V row.
notes.11: RESISTANCE (p. 15, footnote 8): the specifications are for the 4-WIRE ohms function, or the 2-wire ohms function using math null for offset. WITHOUT math null add 0.2 ohm in the 2-wire ohms function: stored as the separate function "Resistance [2-wire, no math null]" with a fixed 0.2 ohm term (a plain lookup prefers the 4-wire function; pass variant="2-wire"; the main function is named "4-wire or 2W with math null" on purpose, so that variant="2-wire" selects only the no-math-null rows). Footnote 8 also: the 100 Mohm and 1 Gohm ranges are 2-wire ohms function only, and "see the manual for low power ohms specification and measurement currents" (the low-power ohms figures are NOT in the data sheet and NOT stored). Temperature coefficients (not stored, non ACAL / with ACAL): 100 ohm 0.0006 + 0.0005 / 0.0002 + 0.0005, 1 k - 100 k 0.0006 + 0.0001 / 0.0002 + 0.0001, 1 Mohm 0.0010 + 0.0002 / 0.0002 + 0.0002, 10 Mohm 0.0030 + 0.0004 / 0.0030 + 0.0004, 100 Mohm 0.1000 + 0.0001 / 0.0100 + 0.0001, 1 Gohm 1.0000 + 0.0001 / 0.1000 + 0.0001.
notes.12: RESISTANCE 100 Mohm and 1 Gohm (footnote 8): 2-wire function only. OWNER DECISION: the "Resistance [2-wire, no math null]" function ALSO carries these two ranges, with the same figures as the 4-wire / math-null rows and NO 0.2 ohm adder (the 0.2 ohm is negligible against 0.3 % and 3 %, and these ranges exist only as 2-wire). The data sheet itself does not say whether the footnote 8 adder applies to them: the choice is the owner's, not a printed fact.
notes.13: DC CURRENT (p. 15): ranges 1 uA to 10 A; burden voltage at full scale (p. 16, information): 1 uA < 0.0011 V, 10 uA < 0.011 V, 100 uA < 0.11 V, 1 mA < 0.11 V, 10 mA < 0.027 V, 100 mA < 0.27 V, 1 A < 0.7 V / 0.05 V, 3 A < 2.0 V / 0.15 V (the second value is obtained on the 10 A input, footnote 21), 10 A < 0.5 V. Temperature coefficients (not stored): 1 uA 0.0020 + 0.0010, 10 uA 0.0015 + 0.0006, 100 uA 0.0015 + 0.0004, 1 mA 0.0015 + 0.0005, 10 mA 0.0020 + 0.0020, 100 mA 0.0020 + 0.0005, 1 A 0.0050 + 0.0010, 3 A 0.0050 + 0.0020, 10 A 0.0050 + 0.0010. The printed 1 mA 24 hour cell reads "0.0070+ 0.0030" (spacing misprint, not stored).
notes.14: DC CURRENT TYPICAL: the 1 uA, 10 uA and 100 uA rows are printed "(typ)" - typical, not warranted; the labels say so.
notes.15: CURRENT 10 A range (footnote 4): only available on a separate front panel connector. Add 2 mA base per amp for inputs greater than 5 Arms. NOT in the stored 10 A rows (DC and AC). The 3 A and 10 A ranges have no 20 % over range (footnote 2).
notes.16: TRUE RMS AC VOLTAGE (p. 16): 100 mV, 1 V, 10 V, 100 V and 750 V ranges share one table; footnote 14: sine wave input > 0.3 % of range and > 1 mVrms; 750 V range limited to 8 x 10^7 V.Hz; for each additional volt over 300 Vrms add 1 mVrms of error (NOT stored); footnote 15: slow filter (3 Hz, 20 Hz, 200 Hz) low-frequency performance. Temperature coefficients (not stored, add per degC outside TCAL +/- 5 degC, footnote 5): 3-5 Hz 0.010 + 0.003, 5-10 Hz 0.008 + 0.003, 10 Hz-20 kHz 0.007 + 0.003, 20-50 kHz 0.010 + 0.005, 50-100 kHz 0.060 + 0.008, 100-300 kHz 0.200 + 0.020. A band edge belongs to both bands; the larger limit is used there (repository rule). The 750 V range has no 20 % over range.
notes.17: TRUE RMS AC CURRENT (p. 16, footnotes 16, 17): sine wave input > 1 % of range and > 10 uArms; specifications are for sine wave input unless stated otherwise. The 5 kHz to 10 kHz band is TYPICAL on every range (labels say so). 100 uA, 1 mA, 10 mA, 100 mA and 1 A share one table; 3 A and 10 A have their own. Temperature coefficients (not stored): 0.015 + 0.006 (3 Hz-5 kHz), 0.030 + 0.006 (5-10 kHz). The 24 hour and 90 day cells of the 100 uA - 1 A group differ (0.07 / 0.09) from the 1 year / 2 year cells (0.10): stored as printed.
notes.18: CAPACITANCE (p. 16): 1 nF to 100 uF, % of reading + % of range, the same figure in the 90 day, 1 year and 2 year columns (temperature coefficients 0.05 + 0.05 for 1 nF, 0.05 + 0.01 for the rest; not stored). Footnote 20: for using Math Null zeroing; high dissipation factor capacitors may show different results than a single frequency measurement; film capacitors usually have lower dissipation factors. The printed superscript on the Capacitance heading is 21 (footnote 21 is about burden voltage): the data sheet's footnote numbering is shifted here; footnote 20 is read as the capacitance one (UNVERIFIED). Rows are stored as bipolar value ranges like every sheet.
notes.19: FREQUENCY (p. 16): % of reading, 100 mV, 1 V, 10 V, 100 V and 750 V ranges; footnote 19 (printed superscript 18, 20): input > 100 mV; for 10 mV to 100 mV inputs multiply the % of reading error by 10; amplitude 10 % - 120 % of range except 14 % - 100 % for 750 ACV; 1 second gate time (7 digits). Stored by frequency band only. Temperature coefficient: 0.0002 (% of reading per degC) for every band (not stored). The footnote numbering of this section is shifted in the data sheet (see note 18): UNVERIFIED which footnote belongs to which heading.
notes.20: FREQUENCY square wave (footnote 18): square wave input specified for 10 Hz to 300 kHz for a 1 second aperture; for shorter apertures the minimum frequency requires > 2 cycles. Stored as the separate function "Frequency [Square wave]" (variant="square"). Additional frequency errors (% of reading, NOT stored; by aperture 1 s (0.1 ppm) / 0.1 s (1 ppm) / 0.01 s (10 ppm) / 0.001 s (100 ppm)): 3-40 Hz 0 / 0.100 / 0.160 / 0.160; 40-100 Hz 0 / 0.030 / 0.160 / 0.160; 100 Hz-1 kHz 0 / 0.020 / 0.200 / 0.200; 1 kHz-300 kHz 0 / 0.004 / 0.030 / 0.240; square wave 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.003.
notes.21: NOT STORED: 24 hour column; continuity (1 kohm) and diode test (5 V) rows; DC:DC ratio (typical: normalized input accuracy + normalized reference accuracy); digitizing (typical SFDR / SNDR / bandwidth, p. 17); temperature (p. 15, footnote 12 "limited by the selected probe"): PT100 "Probe accuracy + 0.05 degC", thermistor "Probe accuracy + 0.1 degC", K, J, T, E, N thermocouples "Probe accuracy + reference junction accuracy + 0.3 degC", R thermocouple (250 to 1760 degC) "+ 0.5 degC". They need the probe's own (and the reference junction's, typically +/- 1.0 degC with the U1180A, footnote 13) accuracy, so no number can be stored for the DMM alone. The footnote superscripts 13 / 14 / 23 on the PT100, R thermocouple and thermistor lines do not match the footnote texts well; not used.
